webflow: Site settings → SEO → robots.txt. Delete the “Disallow: /” line, save and publish.
fix: Remove the “Disallow: /” line under “User-agent: *” in robots.txt and publish.
why: A leftover “Disallow: /” keeps the whole site out of search. Remove it from robots.txt.
title: robots.txt blocks every crawler

fix: Make /robots.txt answer with the file, or with a plain 404 if there is none. This is a server or hosting setting.
why: Crawlers treat a server error on robots.txt as “stay out of everything”. It must answer with the file or a plain 404.
title: robots.txt answers with a server error

webflow: Page settings → SEO settings → turn Sitemap indexing on. If the tag is still there, look for a robots meta tag in Page settings → Custom code.
fix: Remove the noindex from the robots meta tag or the X-Robots-Tag header on every page that should be found.
why: A noindex tag or header tells search engines to drop the page. It is often left on from staging.
passed: No page is hidden from search engines
title: Pages are set to noindex

webflow: Site settings → SEO → Sitemap. With auto-generate on, publish again to rebuild it. A sitemap written by hand has to be edited by hand.
fix: Remove the dead addresses from the sitemap, or restore the pages or redirect them.
title: Sitemap lists pages that do not load
why: Search engines are being sent to pages that return an error. Remove them from the sitemap or restore the pages.

title: Sitemap lists pages on another domain
webflow: Site settings → Publishing → Production. Set the live domain as the default, then publish so the sitemap is rebuilt with it.
why: A sitemap should only list this site's own pages. Other domains here usually mean it was generated on staging.
fix: Generate the sitemap on the live domain so every address in it belongs to this site.

title: A sitemap file lists more than 50,000 pages
passed: Sitemap files are within the size limit
why: Search engines stop reading a sitemap file at 50,000 addresses. Split it and list the parts in a sitemap index.
fix: Split the sitemap into files of at most 50,000 addresses and list them in a sitemap index.

why: Links, canonicals or share images that point at a staging address will send visitors and search engines to the wrong site.
fix: Replace every staging address with the live one: canonicals, share images, og:url and links typed in by hand.
webflow: Site settings → SEO → Global canonical tag URL: enter the live domain. For links, pick the page in the link settings instead of pasting a webflow.io address.
title: Pages still point at a staging domain

fix: Point each canonical at the page's own address on this domain.
passed: Canonical tags stay on this domain
why: A canonical on another domain tells search engines the real page lives there, and this one gets dropped.
title: Canonical tags point to another domain
webflow: Site settings → SEO → Global canonical tag URL: enter the live domain, with https and without a trailing slash.

fix: Give every page a title that says what the page is, in about 60 characters.
title: Pages have no title
webflow: Page settings → SEO settings → Title tag. For Collection pages, set it once on the template page and build it from a field.
why: The title is the headline of a search result. Without one, search engines make something up.

title: Broken links between pages
fix: Correct each link, or redirect the missing address to the page that replaced it.
webflow: Fix the link where it is used. If the address used to exist, add it under Site settings → Publishing → 301 redirects.
why: These links go to pages on this site that do not load.

title: Images do not load
fix: Upload the missing files again, or correct the addresses the pages ask for.
why: These image addresses return an error, so visitors see a gap or a broken icon.

fix: Point og:image at an image that loads, using its full address.
title: Share images do not load
why: The og:image address returns an error, so shared links will show no picture.
webflow: Page settings → Open Graph settings → Open Graph image URL.
Site settings → SEO → Sitemap. Turn on Auto-generate sitemap and publish.
title: No sitemap found
fix: Publish a sitemap at /sitemap.xml that lists every page meant to be found.
why: A sitemap tells search engines which pages exist. Publish one at /sitemap.xml and name it in robots.txt.
List the final address of each page, not one that redirects to it.
fix: List the address each redirect ends at, and drop the one that redirects.
title: Sitemap lists pages that redirect
Sitemap lists pages that robots.txt blocks
why: The sitemap invites crawlers to pages robots.txt turns them away from. Decide which one is right.
fix: Either take the pages out of the sitemap or remove the robots.txt rule that blocks them.
passed: robots.txt blocks nothing in the sitemap

title: Sitemap lists pages whose canonical is another page
why: A sitemap should list the canonical address of each page. These pages say the real one is elsewhere.
fix: List only canonical addresses in the sitemap, or correct the canonical tags if they are the mistake.
passed: Every sitemap page is its own canonical
Every page is linked from another page
why: These pages are in the sitemap, but no page that was read links to them. Visitors cannot reach them and search engines give them little weight.
fix: Link to each page from somewhere a visitor would look for it: the navigation, the footer or a related page.
title: Pages that nothing links to

fix: Send the page's content in the HTML itself, by rendering it on the server or building it ahead of time.
passed: Pages carry their content in the HTML
why: The HTML the server sends has almost no text, only a mount point for a script. Crawlers and AI assistants that do not run JavaScript see a blank page.
title: Pages are empty until JavaScript runs
Pages repeat a tag that should appear once
why: With two titles, descriptions or canonicals in one page, it is a toss-up which one a search engine reads.
fix: Keep one title, one meta description and one canonical per page, and delete the extras.
passed: No repeated title, description or canonical tags
webflow: Webflow writes these tags from the SEO settings. Delete the copy pasted into Page settings → Custom code → Inside <head> tag, or Site settings → Custom code → Head code when it is on every page.

why: Pages with the same title compete with each other and look identical in search results.
title: Pages share the same title
fix: Write a title for each page that only that page could have.
webflow: Page settings → SEO settings → Title tag. For Collection pages, set it once on the template page and build it from a field.

title: Pages have no meta description
webflow: Page settings → SEO settings → Meta description. For Collection pages, set it once on the template page and build it from a field.
why: The description is the text under the title in a search result. Without one, search engines pick a snippet themselves.
passed: Every page has a meta description
fix: Write a description of 50 to 160 characters for each page.
Write a description for each page that says what is on that page.
webflow: Page settings → SEO settings → Meta description. For Collection pages, set it once on the template page and build it from a field.
title: Pages share the same meta description
why: A description copied across pages says nothing about any one of them.
A canonical tag names the one true address of a page, so tracking parameters and duplicates do not split its ranking.
title: Pages have no canonical tag
fix: Add a canonical tag to every page, pointing at the page's own address.
webflow: Site settings → SEO → Global canonical tag URL: enter the live domain. Webflow then adds a canonical to every page.
passed: Every page has a canonical tag

title: Pages have no H1
webflow: Select the heading on the canvas and change its tag in the Settings panel. Choose H1 for the main one.
fix: Make the main heading of each page an H1.
why: The H1 is the page's main heading, for readers and search engines alike.
Without a charset, browsers guess, and accented letters and symbols can turn into gibberish.
fix: Add <meta charset="utf-8"> as the first thing in the head.
passed: Every page declares a character set
title: Pages do not declare a character set

passed: No page is set to nofollow
webflow: Look for a robots meta tag in Page settings → Custom code → Inside <head> tag, or Site settings → Custom code → Head code when it is on every page.
why: A page-level nofollow stops search engines passing through to the pages it links to.
title: Pages tell crawlers not to follow their links
fix: Remove nofollow from the robots meta tag or the X-Robots-Tag header.
Remove the meta refresh tag and redirect the address on the server with a 301.
why: A meta refresh is a slow, unreliable redirect. Use a server-side 301 instead.
webflow: Delete the tag from the page's custom code and add the address under Site settings → Publishing → 301 redirects.
title: Pages redirect with a meta refresh
Redirects that pass through more than one hop
why: Each extra hop slows the visitor down and wastes crawl budget. Point the first address straight at the last.
fix: Change the first redirect so it points straight at the final address.
webflow: Site settings → Publishing → 301 redirects. Edit the rule for the first address so its target is the last one.

fix: Give each link words, or an aria-label when it only holds an icon.
why: A link with no words and no image description tells neither a screen reader nor a search engine where it leads.
title: Links have no text
passed: Every link says where it goes
webflow: Select the link, open the Settings panel and add a custom attribute named aria-label that says where it goes.

title: Pages have no share image
passed: Every page has a share image
webflow: Page settings → Open Graph settings → Open Graph image URL.
fix: Add an og:image to every page: 1200 by 630 pixels works everywhere.
why: Without an og:image, links shared on social apps and in chats show a blank card.

title: Images have no alt text
passed: Every image has an alt attribute
fix: Describe each image in a short phrase. Give purely decorative images an empty alt.
webflow: Select the image, open Image settings and fill in Alt text. Setting it on the file in the Assets panel covers every place the image is used.
why: Alt text is what screen readers speak and what search engines read. Decorative images should have an empty alt, not a missing one.
Images this large slow the page noticeably, most of all on phones. Resize or recompress them.
title: Images over 500 KB
fix: Resize each image to the size it is shown at and save it as WebP or AVIF.
webflow: Assets panel → select the image → Compress, which converts it to WebP or AVIF. Resize very large originals before uploading.

title: Pages have no viewport tag
passed: Every page has a viewport tag
fix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> to the head.
why: Without a viewport tag the page renders zoomed out on phones, and Google indexes the mobile version.

title: Broken links to other sites
passed: No broken links to other sites
why: These links go to pages on other sites that no longer exist.
fix: Link to where the page moved, or remove the link.
Change each http:// address to https://, or host the file yourself if its server has no https.
title: Pages load files over plain http
why: Browsers block or flag http files on an https page.

title: Placeholder text left in
fix: Replace the placeholder with real words, or delete the element.
why: “Lorem ipsum” is still on the page.
Visitors and links using the old http address should land on the secure one.
title: http:// does not redirect to https://
fix: Redirect every http:// address to its https:// twin with a 301. This is a hosting setting.
Send a Strict-Transport-Security header with a max-age of at least a year. This is a server or hosting setting.
why: This header tells browsers to always use https for the site, closing the gap where a first visit can be intercepted.
title: No Strict-Transport-Security header

why: Two addresses serving the same pages split links and ranking between them. Redirect one to the other.
fix: Pick www or non-www as the one address and redirect the other to it with a 301.
passed: www and non-www resolve to one address
webflow: Site settings → Publishing → Production. Make one domain the default; Webflow redirects the others to it.
title: The site answers on both www and non-www

fix: Make addresses that do not exist answer with a 404 status, not with a normal page.
why: An address that does not exist should say so with a 404 status, or search engines index error pages as real content.
title: Missing pages do not return a 404

passed: No page is over 2 MB of HTML
why: Googlebot reads only the first 2 MB of a page's HTML. Anything after that, including structured data, is not indexed.
title: Pages over 2 MB of HTML
fix: Move inline scripts, styles and data out of the HTML into separate files.

title: Pages are sent uncompressed
fix: Turn on gzip or Brotli for HTML on the server or the CDN.
why: Turning on gzip or Brotli on the server typically cuts HTML to a quarter of its size.

webflow: The script is usually in Page settings → Custom code → Inside <head> tag, or Site settings → Custom code → Head code when it is on every page.
fix: Correct the JSON: look for a missing comma, quote or bracket, then run it through a validator.
why: A JSON-LD block with a syntax error is ignored entirely, along with any rich result it would have earned.
title: Structured data that cannot be read

fix: Add the properties named in the findings to the markup.
webflow: The script is usually in Page settings → Custom code → Inside <head> tag, or Site settings → Custom code → Head code when it is on every page.
passed: Structured data has its required properties
why: Without these properties the markup does not qualify for the rich result it describes.
title: Structured data is missing required properties

webflow: The script is usually in Page settings → Custom code → Inside <head> tag, or Site settings → Custom code → Head code when it is on every page.
why: Values like “[Business Name]” were never filled in.
title: Structured data still has template placeholders
fix: Replace each bracketed placeholder with the real value.

webflow: Site settings → SEO → robots.txt. Remove the rules for these crawlers, save and publish.
fix: Remove the Disallow rules for these crawlers from robots.txt, or allow them by name.
title: robots.txt blocks AI search crawlers
why: These crawlers fetch pages to answer questions in ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity and to cite sources. Blocking them keeps the site out of those answers. Crawlers that only gather training data are a separate choice and are not flagged.

title: llms.txt is not in the expected format
why: An llms.txt should open with a “# Title” line and list pages as Markdown links.
fix: Start the file with a “# Title” line and list the pages that matter as Markdown links.

why: The language must be a two-letter ISO 639-1 code and the region a two-letter ISO 3166-1 code, as in en-GB. Invalid tags are ignored.
title: Hreflang tags use codes that do not exist
fix: Use a two-letter language code, with a two-letter region after a hyphen when one is needed, as in en-GB.

title: Hreflang sets do not include the page itself
why: Each page must list itself among its language versions, or the whole set can be disregarded.
fix: Add a hreflang tag on each page that points at the page itself.
passed: Every hreflang set includes the page itself

fix: Correct the sitemap address in robots.txt or in the index, or publish the missing file.
why: robots.txt or a sitemap index points at a sitemap file that answers with an error or is not a sitemap. Pages listed only there go unannounced.
title: A sitemap that is named does not load
webflow: Site settings → SEO → robots.txt. Check the Sitemap line. With Auto-generate sitemap on, the file is at /sitemap.xml.

why: Google draws a page before judging it. With the files that style and build it blocked, what it sees is a broken page.
passed: robots.txt lets crawlers load stylesheets and scripts
fix: Remove the Disallow rules that cover CSS and JavaScript files.
webflow: Site settings → SEO → robots.txt. Remove the rules, save and publish.
title: robots.txt blocks stylesheets or scripts

fix: Point each canonical at the final address of a page that loads and may be indexed.
passed: Canonical tags point at pages that load
why: A canonical names the address to index. One that redirects, errors or is set to noindex leaves search engines to guess.
webflow: Site settings → SEO → Global canonical tag URL: enter the live domain exactly as it is served, with or without www.
title: Canonical tags point at pages that redirect or do not load

webflow: To drop a page, add its address under Site settings → Publishing → 301 redirects.
fix: Keep one of the pages and redirect the others to it, or give each page its own words.
passed: No two pages have the same text
why: Two addresses carrying the same words compete with each other, and search engines keep only one of them.
title: Pages with exactly the same text

fix: Correct or remove the dead links in /llms.txt.
title: llms.txt links to pages that do not load
why: The file exists to point assistants at the pages that matter. A dead link there points them at nothing.

passed: Hreflang tags are only on canonical pages
fix: Put the hreflang tags on the canonical page, or correct the canonical if it is the mistake.
why: Search engines read hreflang from the canonical page only. On a page that names another as its canonical, the tags are ignored.
title: Hreflang tags sit on pages whose canonical is another page

fix: Point each hreflang link at the final address of a page that loads and is not set to noindex.
why: Each language version has to be a page that loads and may be indexed, or that language drops out of the set.
title: Hreflang links point at pages that redirect, do not load or are noindex
passed: Hreflang links point at pages that load

title: Hreflang sets name a language twice
fix: Keep one address for each language and region, and delete the other tag.
passed: Each language appears once in a hreflang set
webflow: Webflow Localization writes hreflang tags itself. Delete any typed by hand in Page settings → Custom code → Inside <head> tag, or Site settings → Custom code → Head code when it is on every page.
why: Two different pages claiming the same language and region leave search engines to pick one, or neither.
If page A names B as its translation, B must name A back. One-way links are ignored.
fix: Add the missing tag on the other page, so each language version names all the others.
title: Hreflang links are not returned

fix: Publish a robots.txt that allows crawlers in and names the sitemap.
title: No robots.txt
why: Not required, but it is where crawlers look first and where the sitemap is announced.
webflow: Site settings → SEO → robots.txt. Enter the rules, save and publish.

fix: Add a line to robots.txt: “Sitemap:” followed by the sitemap's full address.
why: A “Sitemap:” line in robots.txt lets every crawler find it without being told.
title: robots.txt does not name the sitemap
webflow: Site settings → SEO → robots.txt. Add the Sitemap line, save and publish.

why: Identical dates mean the sitemap stamps the build time on everything, so search engines learn to ignore them.
title: Every sitemap entry has the same last-modified date
fix: Write the date each page really changed, or leave lastmod out.

title: Sitemap lists pages set to noindex
fix: Take the noindex off the pages that should be found, and take the rest out of the sitemap.
webflow: Page settings → SEO settings → Sitemap indexing decides both at once for a page.
passed: No noindex pages in the sitemap
why: A sitemap asks for pages to be indexed; noindex asks for the opposite. Remove one or the other.

title: Linked pages are missing from the sitemap
why: These pages are linked from the site and load fine, but the sitemap does not mention them.
fix: Add the pages to the sitemap, or regenerate it.
passed: Linked pages are all in the sitemap
Every page is within three clicks of home
fix: Link to the page from somewhere nearer the home page: a hub page, the navigation or the footer.
why: The further a page is from the home page, the less often it is crawled and the less weight it carries.
title: Pages more than three clicks from the home page

why: Link to the final address. It saves visitors a round trip and keeps the link's full value.
fix: Change each link to the address the redirect ends at.
passed: Links between pages go straight there
title: Links between pages go through a redirect
Redirects marked as temporary
why: A 302 or 307 says the move is temporary, so search engines keep the old address. Use a 301 for a move that is meant to last.
fix: Change the redirect to a 301 if the move is permanent.

why: Words like “click here” or “read more” waste the one place a link can say what it leads to.
fix: Reword each link so it says where it goes.
title: Links that just say “click here”

why: These links leave a secure page for an insecure address. Most destinations have an https version.
fix: Change each link to https:// where the other site has it.
title: Links to http:// addresses

webflow: Page settings → Slug. Then add the old address under Site settings → Publishing → 301 redirects.
why: Capital letters, underscores, doubled slashes and very long addresses are harder to share and easier to mistype.
title: Addresses that are long or untidy
fix: Use short lowercase addresses with hyphens between words, and redirect the old address when one changes.

webflow: Page settings → SEO settings → Title tag. For Collection pages, set it once on the template page and build it from a field.
why: Search results show roughly 60 characters. Longer titles get cut off; very short ones waste the space.
title: Titles are very short or very long
fix: Aim for 10 to 60 characters, with the words that matter first.

why: Search results show roughly 160 characters. Aim for 50 to 160.
passed: Meta descriptions are a sensible length
webflow: Page settings → SEO settings → Meta description. For Collection pages, set it once on the template page and build it from a field.
title: Meta descriptions are very short or very long
fix: Aim for 50 to 160 characters.
If it is not deliberate, point the canonical at the page's own address.
why: This can be deliberate. If it is not, the page is telling search engines to index a different one instead.
title: Canonical tags point to a different page

why: One main heading per page keeps the outline clear.
webflow: Select the heading on the canvas and change its tag in the Settings panel.
title: Pages have more than one H1
passed: No page has more than one H1
fix: Keep one H1 and make the others H2.

title: Headings skip a level
passed: Headings step down one level at a time
why: An H2 followed by an H4 leaves a hole in the outline that screen readers and AI summaries rely on.
fix: Step headings down one level at a time. Choose the tag for the outline and style it to look however it should.
webflow: Select the heading on the canvas and change its tag in the Settings panel.

fix: Add what a visitor would come to this page to find out, or leave it if the page is meant to be short.
title: Pages with under 200 words
passed: Every page has at least 200 words
why: There is little here for a search engine to rank. Fine for a contact page, a problem for a page meant to be found.

fix: Start the file with <!doctype html>.
why: Without <!doctype html> browsers fall back to a legacy rendering mode.
title: Pages have no doctype

webflow: Page settings → Open Graph settings. Fill in the title and description, or tick the boxes that reuse the SEO ones.
passed: Every page has a share title and description
title: Pages are missing share titles or descriptions
fix: Add og:title and og:description to every page.
why: og:title and og:description control the text on a shared link.

webflow: Site settings → Custom code → Head code. Paste the tag there so every page has it.
title: Pages have no Twitter card tag
passed: Every page has a Twitter card tag
fix: Add <meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image"> to the head.
why: A twitter:card tag chooses between a small thumbnail and a large image when the link is posted on X.
Shares and likes are counted against og:url. If it differs from the canonical they are credited to a different address.
fix: Set og:url to the same address as the canonical.
title: og:url differs from the canonical
Images over 200 KB
webflow: Assets panel → select the image → Compress, which converts it to WebP or AVIF. Resize very large originals before uploading.
fix: Resize each image to the size it is shown at and save it as WebP or AVIF.
why: Worth a second look: most content images can be well under 200 KB in a modern format.

title: Images have no width and height
passed: Every image has a width and height
fix: Add width and height attributes to each image, matching the file's proportions.
why: Without both attributes the browser cannot reserve space, so the page jumps as images arrive.
A filename, a single generic word or a paragraph is not a description. Aim for a short phrase saying what the image shows.
title: Alt text that says nothing
fix: Rewrite the alt text as a short phrase that says what the image shows.
webflow: Select the image, open Image settings and fill in Alt text. Setting it on the file in the Assets panel covers every place the image is used.

title: The first image on the page is lazy-loaded
webflow: Select the image, open Image settings and set Load to Eager.
why: Lazy-loading the first image usually delays the largest thing on screen. Keep lazy loading for images further down.
fix: Remove loading="lazy" from the first image on the page.
Look at caching and hosting first: a page served from a cache near the visitor answers in well under a second.
passed: Pages start answering within a second
why: The server took over a second to begin its reply, measured from this Mac. Everything else on the page waits on that.
title: Pages are slow to start answering

passed: No render-blocking scripts in the head
fix: Add defer or async to the script tag, or move it to the end of the body.
webflow: Site settings → Custom code. Add defer to the tag in Head code, or move it to Footer code.
why: A script in the head without async or defer stops the page drawing until it has downloaded and run.
title: Scripts in the head hold up the page

why: Not a ranking factor, but each of these closes off a common attack on visitors.
fix: Set the missing headers on the server or the CDN.
title: Recommended security headers are missing

webflow: Paste the script into Page settings → Custom code → Inside <head> tag, or Site settings → Custom code → Head code when it is on every page.
title: No structured data on the site
fix: Add a JSON-LD script describing the organisation to the home page, then the type that fits each kind of page.
why: Schema.org markup tells search engines what a page is (an organisation, an article, a product) and unlocks rich results.

webflow: The script is usually in Page settings → Custom code → Inside <head> tag, or Site settings → Custom code → Head code when it is on every page. On a Collection template, fill the values from fields.
passed: Structured data has its recommended properties
title: Structured data is missing recommended properties
fix: Add the properties named in the findings where the page has something to put in them. Leave out any that do not apply.
why: The markup is read without these, but they are what puts a logo, a date or an author beside the result. Each one missing is a chance left open.

webflow: The script is usually in Page settings → Custom code → Inside <head> tag, or Site settings → Custom code → Head code when it is on every page.
fix: Remove the retired types, or leave them: they do no harm.
why: Search engines have stopped showing rich results for these types. They do no harm, but they no longer do any good.
title: Structured data types that no longer earn a rich result

fix: Optional. Publish a Markdown file at /llms.txt with a “# Title” line and links to the pages that matter.
title: No llms.txt
why: An optional Markdown file at /llms.txt that points AI assistants at the pages that matter. Search engines ignore it.
x-default names the page for visitors whose language is not listed.
title: Hreflang sets have no x-default
fix: Add a hreflang="x-default" tag to each set, pointing at the version to show everyone else.
Write each date as YYYY-MM-DD, the day the page last changed, and never later than today.
why: A last-modified date has to be a day that has happened, written as 2026-02-07. Search engines stop trusting a sitemap whose dates cannot be true.
title: Sitemap dates are in the future or are not dates
Pages forbid search snippets
why: nosnippet or max-snippet:0 shows the page in search with no description, and keeps it out of AI answers. Sometimes deliberate, rarely wanted on a marketing page.
fix: Remove nosnippet and max-snippet:0 from the robots meta tag, unless the page is meant to show with no description.
webflow: Look for a robots meta tag in Page settings → Custom code → Inside <head> tag, or Site settings → Custom code → Head code when it is on every page.

title: Pages stop visitors zooming
fix: Use <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> and leave out user-scalable and maximum-scale.
why: user-scalable=no or a maximum-scale of 1 stops people enlarging text they cannot read.

fix: Give the date in a <time datetime> element, an article:published_time tag, or datePublished in the page's JSON-LD.
title: Articles show no date
why: These pages say they are articles but give no publication date in the markup. Readers, search engines and AI assistants all weigh how fresh an article is.

title: No contact or about page linked from the home page
why: A way to reach the people behind a site is one of the first things a visitor looks for, and one of the first signs of a site that can be trusted.
fix: Link to a contact or about page from the home page, in the navigation or the footer.
passed: The home page links to a contact or about page

fix: Remove the Disallow rules for these agents from robots.txt, or allow them by name.
passed: Assistants may fetch pages for their users
why: When someone pastes a link into ChatGPT, Claude or Perplexity, these agents fetch the page. Blocked, the assistant can say nothing about it.
title: robots.txt blocks assistants fetching pages for their users
webflow: Site settings → SEO → robots.txt. Remove the rules for these agents, save and publish.

fix: Save each image as WebP or AVIF, or serve it through an image service that converts on request.
title: Images are not offered in a modern format
why: These are sent as JPEG or PNG even to a browser that asks for WebP or AVIF, which are typically a third smaller.
webflow: Assets panel → select the image → Compress, which converts it to WebP or AVIF. Resize very large originals before uploading.
passed: Images are offered in a modern format

title: Pages load every image at once
webflow: Select the image, open Image settings and set Load to Lazy.
fix: Add loading="lazy" to the images below the first screen. Leave the first one as it is.
why: With ten or more images and none marked lazy, the browser fetches them all before the visitor has scrolled.
og:image should start with https://. Some apps do not resolve a relative address, and show no picture.
passed: Share images are given as full addresses
fix: Write og:image as a full address, starting with https://.
webflow: Page settings → Open Graph settings → Open Graph image URL.
title: Share images are not given as full addresses

webflow: The script is usually in Page settings → Custom code → Inside <head> tag, or Site settings → Custom code → Head code when it is on every page.
fix: Write dates as YYYY-MM-DD and addresses in full, starting with https://.
title: Structured data has values in the wrong form
why: Dates should be written as 2026-02-07 and addresses in full. A value in another form is skipped, and the property counts as missing.
passed: Structured data values are well formed

why: Every address in a set should use https. A stray http address redirects, and the pair it belongs to stops matching.
fix: Change the http:// addresses in the set to https://.
title: Hreflang sets mix http and https
Pages do not declare a language
webflow: Site settings → General → Localization → Language code.
fix: Add a lang attribute to the <html> tag, such as lang="en".
why: The lang attribute on <html> helps screen readers and translation tools.

title: No favicon
webflow: Site settings → General → Icons → Favicon.
why: The small icon in browser tabs and some search results.
fix: Add a favicon and link to it from the head.
